# Assessment — #563: Network access presets: bundle binding + auth + mDNS into one wizard choice

_Codebase assessment against 0.13.0-beta.3 (2026-07-12). Effort: **L**._

## Current state (already merged)

No preset concept exists anywhere — no wizard step, no SetupSpec field, no CLI flag, no 'preset'/'networkAccess' identifiers in the codebase. What exists are the separate primitives the issue wants to compose. (1) Bind addresses: compose nested defaults are fully wired — packages/skeleton/system/stack/core.compose.yml:90-102 (OP_BIND_ADDRESS, OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS, OP_CLIENT_BIND_ADDRESS with 127.0.0.1 defaults) and portals.compose.yml:148-151 (guardian :3830 on OP_BIND_ADDRESS; chat/api per-service overrides). A binary admin toggle already exists: GET/PUT /api/host/stack (packages/ui/src/routes/api/host/stack/+server.ts:52,88) surfaces OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS as lanExposureEnabled and writes it via patchSecretsEnvFile; AssistantTab.svelte renders it as a 'LAN Exposure' checkbox. (2) Bind warnings: packages/lib/src/control-plane/bind-warning.ts still uses raw env-var wording ('OP_BIND_ADDRESS is set to...'), consumed by the CLI (packages/cli/src/commands/install.ts:148). (3) OpenCode auth: partially plumbed. OP_OPENCODE_PASSWORD has a secret mapping (packages/lib/src/control-plane/secret-mappings.ts:22, secrets.ts:28,131-132), the UI reads OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD for the default endpoint (packages/ui/src/lib/server/endpoints.ts:258), and the connections page documents rotation via stack.env (routes/connections/+page.svelte:230-245, from #486's landed Phase 2). BUT core.compose.yml:54 hardcodes OPENCODE_AUTH: "false" with a comment stating 'Guardian-side upstream auth plumbing has been removed, so enabling assistant auth is not a supported hardening path', and OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD is NOT passed into the assistant container. The assistant entrypoint (containers/assistant/entrypoint.sh:143-185, 503-580) has the OPENCODE_AUTH gate, refuses to start the unauthenticated client co-process on a non-loopback bind, and handles explicit-origin CORS — so the container-side safety logic is real. Guardian's proxy builds a FRESH minimal upstream header set with no Authorization (packages/guardian/src/proxy.ts:92-113), confirming guardian→assistant would break if OpenCode Basic auth were turned on. (4) mDNS: assistant-side native OpenCode responder config ships mdns:false + mdnsDomain openpalm.local in packages/skeleton/system/assistant/opencode.jsonc:49-54 — but that file lives in the MANAGED system/ tree that overwriteSystemTree (packages/lib/src/control-plane/core-assets.ts) blind-overwrites on every install/update, so a preset flipping mdns:true has no persistence mechanism today. docs/technical/network-partitioning-d5a.md documents hard caveats: bridge networking keeps container mDNS off the LAN (needs network_mode:host on Linux; inert on macOS entirely). Guardian mDNS responder (#488) does not exist — zero mdns code in packages/guardian. (5) Wizard: 3 steps (Connect/Add-ons/Finish) in packages/ui/src/routes/setup/+page.svelte driven by setup-state.svelte.ts; the payload contract (packages/ui/src/lib/setup/payload.ts SetupPayload) and lib SetupSpec (packages/lib/src/control-plane/setup.ts:54-72) have no network fields; performSetup (setup.ts:299+) is the natural stack.env write point (already calls patchSecretsEnvFile). ReviewStep already has an editable pre-filled password field (generatePassword) as UX precedent. CLI file-based install feeds a SetupSpec JSON to performSetup (packages/cli/src/commands/install.ts:325-346), so extending SetupSpec covers the CLI path.

## Test strategy

Test-first in three layers matching existing runners. (1) packages/lib uses `bun test` with colocated *.test.ts (packages/lib/package.json script 'test'): write network-preset.test.ts asserting the full 4-row matrix (bind addresses, OPENCODE_AUTH, password presence, mdns flags) before implementing; extend setup.test.ts / install-edge-cases.test.ts (existing makeValidSpec pattern) for the SetupSpec.network field, the shared-guardian hard-pin rejection, and stack.env writes; extend bind-warning.test.ts for the reworded messages; extend network-partitioning.test.ts and skeleton-guardrail.test.ts (pure YAML/JSONC fixture parsing, no Docker) to pin the new OPENCODE_AUTH/OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD compose interpolations and the mdns file-assembly result. Run: `bun test packages/lib`. (2) packages/ui uses vitest with colocated *.vitest.ts (`npm run test:unit` / `vitest` in packages/ui): extend payload.vitest.ts for buildSetupPayload/parseSetupConfig round-tripping the preset + password, setup-state.vitest.ts for the new step state, routes/api/host/stack/server.vitest.ts for preset surfacing, plus a component vitest for the new step (pattern: Screen1ModelsStep.svelte.vitest.ts). (3) guardian upstream auth: bun test packages/guardian — extend proxy.test.ts/proxy-preauth.test.ts to assert Authorization: Basic is attached upstream when the password env/secret is present and absent otherwise. Full sweep: `bun run test` at repo root (root package.json:62 covers cli/lib/guardian and more).

## Dependencies (0.13.0 open issues)

- #488 — hard blocker for the 'Shared network, guardian protected' preset: the guardian mDNS responder does not exist (no mdns code in packages/guardian; native OpenCode mDNS cannot advertise the guardian front door per docs/technical/network-partitioning-d5a.md), so that preset's guardian-mDNS cell cannot be wired until #488 lands. The other three presets are implementable without it if the preset UI ships with shared-network mDNS marked pending.
- #486 — the issue declares itself blocked by #486 (connection model / remote install); #486's connections-page groundwork has landed (ui-runtime-modes-plan.md Phase 2 marked DONE, routes/connections/+page.svelte already documents OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD endpoints), but the issue's scope item to update #486's dev/advanced framing means the two must be coordinated while #486 remains open.
- #557 — related only (explicit non-goal): TLS/CORS posture is orthogonal; a future shared-network + off-LAN combination stacks #557 on top of the shared-guardian preset.

## Risks

- OPENCODE_AUTH is currently declared unsupported: core.compose.yml:45-53 states guardian-side upstream auth plumbing was REMOVED, and guardian's proxy sends no Authorization upstream (packages/guardian/src/proxy.ts buildUpstreamHeaders). Enabling OpenCode Basic auth for the 'home-password' preset without restoring guardian upstream credentials breaks every portal (Discord/Slack/chat/api) — contradicting the issue's 'portals are unaffected' claim, which holds only at the Docker-network level.
- Assistant mDNS 'already works' is optimistic: per docs/technical/network-partitioning-d5a.md, bridge networking keeps the native responder's multicast off the physical LAN (Linux needs network_mode: host, which changes the container's whole port topology), and it is inert on macOS (Docker Desktop/OrbStack) entirely — the wizard must not promise .local discovery it cannot deliver on macOS.
- mDNS config lives in the managed system/assistant/opencode.jsonc that overwriteSystemTree blind-overwrites on every install/update — without a re-assembly step keyed off persisted preset state, a user's mDNS choice silently reverts on the next update.
- Setting the global OP_BIND_ADDRESS=LAN for the shared-guardian preset cascades to chat/api/voice/client ports via the nested compose defaults (portals.compose.yml:150-151, services.compose.yml:110) — the preset writer must explicitly pin every per-service override it does not intend to expose, or the preset exposes more than the matrix says.
- Two write paths for the same env vars (wizard preset vs the existing /api/host/stack lanExposureEnabled toggle vs hand-edited stack.env) can drift; without drift detection the admin UI may show a preset that no longer matches reality.
- The assistant entrypoint's I3 gate refuses to start the client co-process when LAN-bound without auth (entrypoint.sh:174-185) — the 'Home network, open access' preset intentionally hits this path, so the preset either loses the browser client on LAN or the gate semantics need a deliberate, security-reviewed exception; also wildcard-bind + auth requires operators to set OP_CLIENT_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (entrypoint.sh:552-554), which the preset should compute automatically.

## Original issue body

# #563: Network access presets: bundle binding + auth + mDNS into one wizard choice

## Summary

Give the setup wizard (and `openpalm` CLI) a single **network access preset** choice that configures binding addresses, OpenCode auth, and mDNS advertisement together, instead of requiring operators to hand-tune `OP_BIND_ADDRESS` / `OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS` / `OP_OPENCODE_PASSWORD` / mDNS individually.

Spun out of the 0.13.0 review of #486 and #488, once it became clear that "should the guardian or the assistant be mDNS-discoverable" has a real answer that depends on trust level of the network, and that the underlying settings (bind addresses, OpenCode's own Basic auth, mDNS) already exist as separate primitives that just need to be composed.

## Presets

| Preset | Guardian bind (`OP_BIND_ADDRESS`) | Assistant bind (`OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS`) | OpenCode auth (`OPENCODE_AUTH` / `OP_OPENCODE_PASSWORD`) | Guardian mDNS | Assistant mDNS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **This PC only** (default, unchanged) | loopback | loopback | off | off | off |
| **Home network, with password** | loopback | LAN | on — password is user-specified in the wizard (not forced-generated); a strong default can be pre-filled/suggested, but the operator can view/edit it | off | on |
| **Home network, open access** | loopback | LAN | off — explicit risk warning shown in the wizard before enabling | off | on |
| **Shared network, guardian protected** | LAN | loopback — **hard-pinned, never exposed for this preset** | n/a (not exposed) | on | off |

Portals (Discord/Slack) are unaffected by preset choice — they always route through the guardian regardless (already enforced at the Docker network level, `portal_net` has no path to the assistant container).

## Why this needs its own issue

This isn't just an mDNS toggle: it's wizard UI, a bind-address decision matrix, OpenCode auth plumbing that exists (`OP_OPENCODE_PASSWORD`, `OPENCODE_AUTH`, see `docs/technical/auth-and-proxy-refactor-plan.md`) but is currently unused/blank by default, and (for the "Shared network" preset) the guardian mDNS responder from #488.

## Scope

- [ ] Wizard step: preset selector (4 options above) with a plain-language description of what each exposes and to whom
- [ ] Home-network presets: wire `OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS` to LAN, wire `OPENCODE_AUTH`/`OP_OPENCODE_PASSWORD` for the password variant with a user-editable password field (suggest a strong default, don't force-generate silently)
- [ ] Shared-network preset: wire `OP_BIND_ADDRESS` to LAN, hard-pin `OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS` to loopback (validation should refuse to let this preset expose the assistant directly)
- [ ] mDNS wiring per preset, per #488 (assistant mDNS already works; guardian mDNS needs #488's responder)
- [ ] Bind-address warnings (`bind-warning.ts`) reviewed so the wording matches the new preset framing rather than raw env var names
- [ ] Update #486's "dev/advanced only" framing for direct-to-assistant connections — that framing predates this issue; direct assistant access is now a supported preset for home users, not just a dev/advanced path

## Non-goals

- No change to TLS/CORS posture — that's #557, orthogonal to LAN-only presets. A future "shared network + hosted/remote access" combination would still need #557 on top of the "Shared network, guardian protected" preset.
- No multi-preset/custom mode in v1 — advanced users can still hand-set the underlying env vars; presets are a convenience layer, not a restriction.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by **#488** (guardian mDNS responder — needed for the "Shared network, guardian protected" preset)
- Blocked by **#486** (connection model / remote install — the direct-assistant home presets are the local-network case of the same remote-connection story)
- Related: #557 (TLS, for when a shared-network guardian also needs to be reachable off-LAN)
